request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 32.1% (95% band 29.3% to 46.6%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.39; 1: +0.5; >= 2: +2.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.48, 95% band [+2.41, +2.70]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 20.7% (95% band 17.9% to 24.6%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 79999: +0.54; 80000-149999: +0.2; 150000-509999: -0.38; >= 510000: -0.7 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.27, 95% band [-1.47, -0.99]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 9.3% (95% band 5.6% to 10.6%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1239: +0.18; 1240-8294: -0.05; >= 8295: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.65, 95% band [-0.69, -0.32]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 6.8% (95% band 2.4% to 9.2%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.62 (95% band [+0.15, +0.90]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 201,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.8% (95% band 2.7% to 7.2%); rank 4 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.20, 95% band [-0.29, +0.00]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.7% (95% band 0.3% to 4.9%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1843: 0; 1844-3859: +0.1; >= 3860: 0 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.35, 95% band [+0.00, +0.57]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.7% (95% band 0.4% to 4.4%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.10, 95% band [-0.09, +0.19]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 2.8%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.07, 95% band [-0.09, +0.13]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.3% to 2.2%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.06 (95% band [+0.02, +0.13]) from x = 1 (5th percentile) to x = 3 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.

Interactions: the model has 32 pairs. The larger ones:
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 2.2% (95% band 0.0% to 3.2%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.88 (95% band +0.17 to +1.20) when `AGE` = 23, +0.26 (95% band +0.01 to +0.69) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.34 (95% band +0.00 to +0.47) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.28 (95% band -0.49 to +0.12) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 1.1% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.46 (95% band +2.25 to +2.79) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.59 (95% band +2.24 to +2.85) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.16 (95% band -1.44 to -0.88) when `PAY_0` = -2, -1.03 (95% band -1.49 to -0.72) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & AGE`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.0% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.54 (95% band +2.41 to +2.72) when `AGE` = 23, +2.40 (95% band +2.32 to +2.68) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.21 (95% band -0.08 to +0.28) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.07 (95% band -0.20 to +0.16) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.5% to 2.3%).

  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.00 (95% band -0.03 to +0.07) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.44 (95% band +0.15 to +0.64) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.4% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.50 (95% band -1.70 to -1.07) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -1.12 (95% band -1.45 to -0.84) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.82 (95% band -0.98 to -0.42) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.44 (95% band -0.59 to -0.20) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.4% to 2.2%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.26 (95% band +2.12 to +2.62) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.37 (95% band +2.27 to +2.74) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.67 (95% band +0.07 to +0.85) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.78 (95% band +0.24 to +1.05) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.2% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.36 (95% band -1.64 to -1.03) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -1.26 (95% band -1.47 to -0.88) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.28 (95% band -0.52 to -0.03) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.18 (95% band -0.28 to +0.21) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.4% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.34 (95% band +2.27 to +2.61) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +2.60 (95% band +2.40 to +2.79) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.68 (95% band -0.72 to -0.33) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.42 (95% band -0.69 to -0.19) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT2 & AGE`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 1.5%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.16 (95% band -0.29 to +0.05) when `AGE` = 23, -0.24 (95% band -0.39 to +0.00) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.14 (95% band -0.07 to +0.23) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.07 (95% band -0.21 to +0.19) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.2% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.78 (95% band +0.12 to +0.90) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.57 (95% band +0.17 to +0.97) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.65 (95% band -0.85 to -0.35) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.86 (95% band -0.92 to -0.29) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `BILL_AMT2 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.2%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: +0.60 (95% band +0.01 to +0.67) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, +0.20 (95% band -0.05 to +0.57) when `PAY_AMT3` = 17,600.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 17,600: +0.20 (95% band -0.06 to +0.23) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.20 (95% band -0.31 to +0.12) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.0% to 1.4%).

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by repayment status in September 2005, the latest month, which accounts for about a third of its importance (32.1%, with a plausible range of 29.3% to 46.6%)."},{"id":2,"text":"Applicants who were already delayed by two or more months in repayment carry much higher predicted risk, with a strong effect of about 2.2 on the log-odds scale; a one-month delay adds a smaller amount, and paying in full lowers the risk."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount of credit granted (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important driver (20.7%), and higher limits are associated with lower predicted default risk, the effect being about 1.3 log-odds units from the 5th to the 95th percentile."},{"id":4,"text":"Payment amounts in September (PAY_AMT1) and the September bill amount (BILL_AMT1) matter less: larger payments lower predicted risk, while larger bills raise it, but these effects are modest and the bill effect is less precisely estimated."},{"id":5,"text":"The model contains several interactions, the most notable being repayment status with credit limit, age and education, but these are secondary; for example, the effect of repayment status is strong at every limit and age level, so it is not overturned by them."},{"id":6,"text":"Age, the earlier payment and bill amounts, and the July payment have small or unresolved effects, so the data do not settle whether they meaningfully change predicted default risk."},{"id":7,"text":"Overall, the model's predictions rest chiefly on recent repayment behaviour and the size of the credit line, with the remaining features adding comparatively little."}]}
